turns.prompt: Give me a list of proposals to improve the game. We are close to the finish
turns.reply:
Here are my proposals, ordered by what matters most for the finish. I based them on the design docs, the open sections in them and the bot playtest results. I haven't played the current build.

**Before submitting**
1. **Rerun the bot playtest and do one full run on a phone.** The bot results in `lab/playtest/results.json` are from 17 Oct. Since then the work RAM, CPU and input wires layers were reworked, and the coin minigame and the bot's deaths were added. In those old numbers, a bot at noise 0.25 (roughly "a player who knows the game") never finished the whole game. A rerun with `--quick` is cheap and shows whether a real player can reach the end.
2. **Give finishing the game a payoff.** The docs don't say what happens when everything is won, apart from the level 256 switch. A short end screen (layers woken, coins spent, time played, no credits) would give players a clear "I finished it" moment.
3. **Help the first minute.** The maze is the front door and the hardest part for slow reactions. The bot clears it 0 times out of 20 at noise 0.5. Two cheap fixes: point at LAYER DOWN after the first game over, or make the first maze a bit easier (more lives, or slower ghosts on round 1).
4. **Make the submission images.** You need a cover image and screenshots for the ldjam.com page. The Games tile on the event page needs a thumbnail too.

**Cheap polish**
5. **Connect the two "half" layer goals** listed in `layer-deep.md`:
   - Bus: carry the byte you picked up back to the CPU.
   - Game logic: standing on a ghost's target tile pulls that ghost in the maze.
   
   The dots in these two layers are only counted and don't tie to anything the part does.
6. **Check the input wires layer's difficulty.** It's the last deep layer, and the bot cleared it only 60% of the time even with no noise. That's either a fine finale or a wall; the rerun will tell.
7. **Mini-gurke easter egg.** Still only proposed: one pickle per layer, a counter, nothing unlocked. It's small and fits the jam story.
8. **Give the lobby its own sound.** It still uses the cabinet's background sound.

**Robustness**
9. **Test on iOS Safari and a low-end Android.** Check that audio starts on the first tap, the game pauses when the tab is hidden, the boot load time, and the frame rate in the deep layers.
10. **Decide what a reload does to progress.** Unlocked layers are lost on reload (session only). Keeping just "layers woken" in localStorage would go against the "no game state in localStorage" rule, so that's your call.

**Docs, if there's time**
11. **Update the stale sections.** In `master.md`, "Current prototype" is outdated and Pillars and Core loop are still open. In `layer-crt.md`, the slice scope is still marked open even though the layer is built.

My suggestion is 1, 2, 3 and 4 first, then 5 if time is left. Item 1 is the cheapest way to find out how hard the game really is right now. Tell me which ones to build.

Plan usage is low (5-hour 0%, weekly 28%), so all of these fit. Nothing visible changed this turn, so there's nothing to test on the phone. The making-of log update is in PR https://github.com/fischerq/ludumdare60/pull/84.
